page: UpCloud PREMIUM-24xCPU-96GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Premium family. It is equipped with 24 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the AMD EPYC 9575F processor using the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 96 GB of RAM, corresponding to a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided through a bundled 400 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without hardware GPU acceleration.

Benchmark testing displays high raw compute efficiency, with single-core stress-ng performance ranking in the top 10% and multi-core performance falling into the top 25%. Data compression and decompression tasks also show upper-tier results, such as single-threaded gzip compression at 38.53 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 342.1 GB/sec. Across broader synthetic metrics, including Geekbench multi-core, Clang compilation, PassMark CPU tests, and Redis SET throughput, the instance performs consistently within average industry percentiles.

A noticeable performance tradeoff lies within the memory subsystem. While cached read bandwidth reaches 3327.36 GB/sec, uncached large-block write bandwidth drops to 21.35 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25% along with PassMark memory scoring. Additionally, the instance utilizes shared CPU scheduling, which should be considered when sizing for uninterrupted execution cycles.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, this server packages a high core count with proportional memory and bundled high-capacity SSD storage, avoiding separate storage attachment expenses. It is well suited for multi-threaded build environments, CI/CD pipelines, static web serving clusters, batch data transformation, and moderate database workloads.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-24xCPU-96GB is a KVM virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration includes 24 vCPUs across 24 physical cores at 2.0 GHz, 96 GB of system RAM, and 400 GB of local SSD storage without GPU acceleration. It features advanced vector instructions including AVX-512 extensions and cryptographic acceleration. Benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core CPU throughput and strong multi-core decompression capabilities, while overall Geekbench, Redis, and database operations score in the middle tier. Memory write bandwidth represents a performance constraint relative to its high computing throughput. With a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio and integrated local storage, this configuration is suitable for CI/CD compilation workloads, backend web services, ETL processing, and relational database systems.
